title: The Test
coreMove: Raise confidence from local promise to field evidence by testing the checklist across different conditions.
sourcePressure: The source centers on Do-Confirm versus Read-Do, the WHO 19-item checklist, and an eight-hospital test that validates the tool across different hospitals.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says a pilot worked. The real chapter asks whether the checklist survives variation across sites, habits, and pressures.

sourceAnchors.name: WHO 19-item checklist
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar identifies the WHO 19-item checklist as the chapter's tested instrument.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The nineteen items matter because the list is short enough to enter real surgery and specific enough to be tested.

sourceAnchors.name: eight-hospital test
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar says the chapter uses an eight-hospital test as its empirical frame.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The eight-hospital test asks whether the pause can work after the room, the country, and the habits change.

sourceAnchors.name: Do-Confirm versus Read-Do
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar says the chapter turns to Do-Confirm versus Read-Do to clarify how the checklist functions.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Do-Confirm protects skilled action after it happens; Read-Do pulls action through a sequence when sequence itself is the risk.

hook: The real test is the field
tryThisNow: Test your checklist in a new setting

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: Rachel, a multi-site surgical trial coordinator
exampleSpecs.audience: clinical researchers moving from promising design to real evidence
exampleSpecs.stakes: a checklist that worked in one operating room may fail in hospitals with different staffing and habits
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rachel compares the same pause across three sites and marks which failures come from local habit versus the checklist's structure
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three hospital badges lying beside one marked-up checklist

exampleSpecs.domain: Tomas, a regional maternity ward rollout lead
exampleSpecs.audience: health-system operators adapting a safety aid across small and large hospitals
exampleSpecs.stakes: a newborn handoff checklist helps the urban ward but slows the rural night shift
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Tomas keeps the same core checks but tests whether Do-Confirm or Read-Do fits each ward's handoff rhythm
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 3:12 a.m., Tomas watches a rural nurse cover two rooms and the phone

exampleSpecs.domain: Astrid, a mining rescue drill verification lead
exampleSpecs.audience: safety teams deciding whether a checklist works beyond training day
exampleSpecs.stakes: a drill list passes at headquarters but fails underground when radios and dust change the conditions
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Astrid predicts the list will hold, then follows the underground drill and marks the item that cannot be heard over the radio
exampleSpecs.firstImage: grit ticking against the plastic face shield in the mine tunnel

exampleSpecs.domain: Sam, a charity vaccine clinic trial planner
exampleSpecs.audience: public health teams that need proof beyond one successful Saturday
exampleSpecs.stakes: the clinic checklist works in a gym but may break in a mobile van and a senior center
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sam tests the same minimum checks in three clinic formats and records where layout changes threaten consent, cold chain, or observation time
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What would still work if the room disappeared?

exampleSpecs.domain: Luca, a municipal election recount process owner
exampleSpecs.audience: public administrators validating a process under scrutiny
exampleSpecs.stakes: a recount process must work in different precinct rooms with observers, paper ballots, and tired staff
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Luca asks each precinct to run the same ballot-chain check and compare where observers interrupt the sequence
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Run it once with observers talking," Luca says over the sealed ballot boxes

exampleSpecs.domain: Kasia, a cross-border freight inspection pilot lead
exampleSpecs.audience: logistics leaders proving a customs handoff works across ports
exampleSpecs.stakes: one border terminal succeeds while another backs up trucks because drivers, brokers, and inspectors use different rhythms
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Kasia separates the checklist's stable checks from local process noise after comparing two terminals and a rail yard
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Kasia one dawn queue of idling trucks to distrust the first terminal's easy success

skillTargets: evaluate whether a checklist's structure survives context changes

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one checklist that seems to work and name the one different setting where it should be tested before you trust it broadly.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
